unmapped_findings: The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al alloy is only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of its mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (which weakens/embrittles on aging) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (which strengthens on aging). [b0024]

Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al belongs to the single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel class: with an Al content below 5 wt.% a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature, and the TWIP effect is the primary deformation mechanism for this composition range. [b0015, b0031]

The intermediate alloy variants with 2-6 wt.% Al (including 4Al) do not show mechanical properties equivalent to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior; the pronounced aging strengthening is attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides mainly in the 8Al variant. [b0025]

The κ-carbide (L′1₂-type, (Fe,Mn)3AlC) characterization in Fig. 5 (APT/TEM) refers to the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy after 24 h at 600 °C, not to this Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al sample; it is therefore not attributed to this sample. [b0034, figure_005]
